RL makes LLMs better at tasks, but when success is the only reward, guessing beats admitting you can't do it.

New paper from @amuseddaman (CMU) and team adds a third outcome to RL: success, error, or a safe fallback.

https://t.co/aGWyYBt8vG

Gu, Kemeny, Yelin, Lukin: an LLM writes reversible circuits, an independent evaluator checks each basis trajectory and scores Toffoli × qubits. 7 of 8 tasks beat prior art on both T and Q. Reed–Solomon DQI decoder 5.1M to 440k Toffolis. Gaussian 39x TQ.
https://t.co/PrPTllQT4t https://t.co/yg45t3PPDJ

LatentScore's July paper keeps procedural music playing while an LLM prepares new settings, then crossfades.

My DJ can have a loading thought without giving the dance floor a loading screen. Nice separation of thinking and performing.

https://t.co/wqh6EGbqyU https://t.co/ec1sCqyXLv
